title: Chapter 187: Tian Teng Medical School
html:
After Xu Wan left, Chen Ge returned to the Haunted House alone. He still had much to do. He repaired the Pen Spirit’s pen, then buried the rooster beside the attraction. Its body bore no wounds, leaving him unsure what had killed it. Suspecting something from behind the door, he had brought it home rather than risk leaving the corpse elsewhere.

Once his chores were finished, Chen Ge entered the underground parking garage. The Third Sick Hall had been fully recreated opposite Mu Yang High School and occupied twice as much space. With every scenario connected by intersecting paths, the Maze of Terror was beginning to take shape.

He inspected the entire scenario for danger, installed several spare cameras at key locations, and then left.

Mu Yang High School came with two hidden missions, and the Third Sick Hall is a three-star scenario, so it should have more hidden missions. However, I’ve walked through the entire scenario, and there is nothing out of place. Looks like the trigger for these hidden missions isn’t so easily found.

Back in the staff break room, Chen Ge was about to lie down when a message from Inspector Lee arrived. After a moment’s thought, he called him. “Uncle San Bao, I’m fine. There’s no need to worry.”

“Well, at least you’re optimistic.” There were footsteps on the other end. Inspector Lee was walking to a secluded spot before he continued. “I’ve seen the footage from last night. When you saw the trapped victims, you should have called the police already.”

“I understand. I’ll be more careful next time.”

“There’s going to be a next time?” Inspector Lee sighed. “Never mind. I only want you to be careful. I also have two updates. According to your statement, three people were involved in imprisoning the victims. All three remain at large. They are mentally ill and potentially capable of anything, so watch yourself.”

“Okay, I’ll be careful.”

“The second update concerns Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy.” Papers rustled on his end of the call. “We reviewed every man connected to the school five years ago and narrowed the list to twenty-one suspects. We should identify the person who drove that girl to suicide within a week.”

Zhang Ya would finally receive justice. Chen Ge exhaled slowly. “Inspector Lee, after you arrest him, can I have five minutes alone with him?”

“We’ll see about it later, but don’t get your hopes up.” Inspector Lee hung up, and Chen Ge looked at his phone, spacing out until he eventually fell asleep.

…

In a blood-red room, Chen Ge sat on the bed while blood vessels surfaced along his legs. He stared around in confusion, and Men Nan’s voice sounded beside him. “You don’t have much time left.”

He turned to find the boy standing in the room’s center, red lines coursing through his body.

“Men Nan?”

“You don’t have much time left,” the boy repeated without expression. As he prepared to say it a third time, the red lines snapped taut and tore his body to pieces.

“Hey!”

Chen Ge’s eyes flew open. Cold sweat drenched his forehead. It was 3:40 a.m.—the exact time he had emerged from the “door.”

Why did I dream that? Has something happened to Men Nan’s original personality behind the door?Sleep was now impossible. Chen Ge collected his phone, toolbox, and backpack and set out for the Third Sick Hall.

He returned at 5:00 a.m. Dawn had begun to break, yet the hospital remained sinister. Chen Ge climbed over the fence. The police had already broken the Third Sick Hall’s locks, allowing him to head straight for Room 3.

Everything inside looked exactly as he had left it, and his search revealed nothing. Deep in thought, Chen Ge ventured farther into the building. He retrieved the hammer and cleaver hidden the previous night, hurried to the director’s office, and used his tools to pry four blood-red nails from the cabinet’s corners.

They look to be normal iron nails.Chen Ge tore a piece off from the curtain, used it to wrap the nails, and placed it inside his backpack.

Morning had arrived, and much remained to be done. Chen Ge left the hospital, walked until he found a taxi, and returned to New Century Park.

After placing down his backpack, Chen Ge put up a sign for temporary closure and carried a bunch of stuff before hurrying to the city center.

“Third floor, Sheng Yuan International Plaza.” Flyer in hand, Chen Ge waited for the elevator beside a group of excited young men and women chatting among themselves.

“I’m shocked that Tian Teng Medical School decided to come to Jiujiang! When they were stationed at Xing Hai last year, I was so ready to hop on a train to go visit them!”

“Sounds like you’re exaggerating again. Su Su, I hear we also have a good Haunted House, and it’s quite famous online.”

“Don’t buy into online rumors. The Haunted Houses we have only rely on cheap tricks; they’re no competition for Tian Teng Medical School. You’re not an aficionado like myself, so you wouldn’t understand it.”

Su Su was a cute girl around five feet three, with a slender, almost boyish figure. A tall young man beside her asked shyly, “Aren’t all Haunted Houses basically the same?”

“Most Haunted Houses are in it for the money, but Tian Teng Medical School is different; they’re aiming for a real haunting experience. The two are leagues apart.” The girl seemed to be a real Haunted House fan. “You won’t understand it even if I explain it to you. Later, you just stick behind me.”

The girl’s enthusiasm caught Chen Ge’s attention. When the elevator arrived, they all rode to the third floor, where the doors opened onto a hall packed with waiting visitors.

“Tian Teng Medical School is this famous?” Chen Ge had risked life and limb promoting his Haunted House online merely to build its current popularity. Tian Teng Medical School had drawn this crowd through word of mouth alone—an impressive achievement.

“Of course they are! They’re the largest traveling Haunted House in the country. They hired a Japanese designer with more than ten years of experience, and everything from the makeup to the sets is custom-made.” Overhearing him, Su Su patiently explained, “Uncle, the ticket is expensive, but it’s absolutely worth the price. They use sound, light, electricity, even smell. It’s the best Japanese-style Haunted House in the nation.”

“Uncle?” Chen Ge’s mouth twitched. After everything he had seen yesterday, that word somehow still stung. Smoothing his expression, he walked past her and murmured, “I’ve never tried a Japanese-style Haunted House. I wonder how it compares with the Third Sick Hall.”
